# FanFic Lab

> Autonomous Honkai: Star Rail (HSR) fanfiction generator. The DreamWriter agent (LangGraph.js,
> running in-process inside a Next.js app) plans, writes, self-reviews for out-of-character issues,
> summarizes, and delivers a finished fanfic — wrapped in a social reading layer (feed, reader,
> likes/comments/follows, profiles).

This file follows the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) convention: a concise, machine-readable map
of the project for large language models and AI agents.

## About

- Repository: https://github.com/ChanMeng666/fanfic-lab
- Live: https://fanfic-lab.tech
- Stack: Next.js 16 · React 19 · TypeScript 5 · TailwindCSS 4 · Prisma 7 · Neon Postgres + pgvector ·
  Redis (Upstash) · Cloudinary · Stack Auth (= Neon Auth engine) · OpenAI · LangGraph.js (in-process)
- Deploy: single Docker image → DigitalOcean VPS (Traefik/Coolify) → Cloudflare CDN
- License: MIT

## Architecture in one paragraph

A single Next.js deployable. The create page POSTs a prompt to `src/app/api/create/route.ts`, which
streams the in-process compiled LangGraph (`getGraph()` in `src/agent/dreamwriter/graph.ts`) over SSE.
The pipeline is `intent_parser → story_architect → writer → quality_guard → [revision loop ≤2] →
summarize → delivery`. JSON nodes use Zod `withStructuredOutput` (`schemas.ts`); state is checkpointed
in Postgres (unpooled connection); writing is grounded by pgvector RAG over an HSR knowledge pack.
Finished stories save via `src/app/api/stories/route.ts`. Logging is structured JSON (`src/lib/logger.ts`);
errors are typed codes (`src/lib/errors.ts`) mapped to Chinese UI strings at the boundary.

## For agents

Read README → AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md first. The agent runs in-process (no `LANGGRAPH_URL`, no separate
service). Do not reintroduce CopilotKit, hand-rolled JSON parsing, or `console.log`. Do not migrate to
Drizzle/Cloudflare R2/Pulumi or split into microservices without explicit discussion — these were
deliberately deferred (see AGENTS.md → "Deferred architecture decisions"). Prefer the project's own
npm scripts over ad-hoc commands.
